notes.md: - **First Lok Sabha:** duly constituted on **17 April 1952** after the first general elections (25 Oct 1951 – 21 Feb 1952); its first sitting was on **13 May 1952**.

new.s: By which system is the Vice-President of India elected?
o: First-past-the-post system by members of the Lok Sabha
Proportional representation by single transferable vote, by secret ballot
Open ballot by simple majority of both Houses
new.x: The Vice-President is elected by MPs of both Houses through PR-STV, and voting is by secret ballot.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: VP election by PR-STV, secret ballot

new.s: Under which Act are the elections to the offices of President and Vice-President of India held?
new.x: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 governs these elections.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: Presidential and VP Elections Act 1952

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India?
new.x: Article 63 creates the office of Vice-President; Article 64 makes him ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: Article 63 office of VP

new.s: On the resignation of the President, whom must the Vice-President inform immediately under Article 56(2)?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
new.x: Article 56(2) requires the Vice-President to communicate the President's resignation at once to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: VP informs Speaker of President's resignation

new.s: Who acted as President of India after Dr. Zakir Husain died in office in 1969?
new.x: Zakir Husain was the first President to die in office; Vice-President V.V. Giri then acted as President.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: V.V. Giri acting President 1969

new.s: Who was the first Prime Minister of India to be a member of the Rajya Sabha?
new.x: Indira Gandhi was a Rajya Sabha member when she became Prime Minister in 1966 - the first PM from the Rajya Sabha.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: first PM from Rajya Sabha

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Indira Gandhi was the first woman Prime Minister of India.
2. Indira Gandhi was the first Prime Minister from the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Indira Gandhi (1966) was both the first woman PM and the first PM who was a Rajya Sabha member.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: Indira Gandhi first woman PM / first RS PM

new.s: Under which Act was the National Disaster Management Authority, chaired by the Prime Minister, set up?
new.x: The NDMA, headed by the Prime Minister, was set up under the Disaster Management Act of 23 December 2005.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: NDMA - Disaster Management Act 2005

new.s: In which year was the Gandhi Peace Prize instituted?
new.x: The Gandhi Peace Prize was started in 1995, Gandhi's 125th birth anniversary year.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: Gandhi Peace Prize started 1995

new.s: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor of a State?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court concerned
The Chief Minister of the State
new.x: Under Article 159 the Governor takes oath before the Chief Justice of the High Court of the State.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: Governor's oath by HC Chief Justice

new.s: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
new.x: Under Article 60 the President takes oath before the Chief Justice of India.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: President's oath by CJI

new.s: Which Articles of the Constitution does the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 touch?
new.x: The Bill, on removing a PM/CM/Minister detained for 30 days, touches Articles 75 (Union), 164 (States) and 239AA (Delhi).
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: 130th Amendment Bill - Articles 75, 164, 239AA

new.s: In July 2025, Narendra Modi's continuous tenure as Prime Minister went past that of which Prime Minister?
new.x: In July 2025 Modi passed Indira Gandhi's continuous tenure; Nehru still holds the record.
new.angle: U0301 notes gap: Modi passes Indira Gandhi's continuous tenure (2025)

new.s: On which model is India's parliamentary system of government based?
new.x: India's cabinet or responsible government follows the British Westminster model, as do Japan and Canada.
new.angle: U0302 notes gap: Westminster model

new.s: Who chairs the Civil Services Board at the Centre?
new.x: The Cabinet Secretary, the senior-most civil servant, chairs the Civil Services Board.
new.angle: U0302 notes gap: Cabinet Secretary chairs Civil Services Board

new.s: Up to what maximum total term can the tenure of the Cabinet Secretary be extended?
new.x: The Cabinet Secretary is appointed by the ACC for 2 years, extendable up to 4 years.
new.angle: U0302 notes gap: Cabinet Secretary term extendable to 4 years

new.s: Who is the Union Home Secretary whose tenure was extended in August 2026?
new.x: In August 2026 Home Secretary Govind Mohan's tenure was extended up to 22.8.2027.
new.angle: U0302 notes gap: Home Secretary Govind Mohan extension (2026)

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Attorney General of India?
o: He may take up private practice
He has the right of audience in all courts in India
He is a member of the Union Cabinet
He holds office during the pleasure of the President
new.x: The Attorney General is not a member of the Cabinet; he is not a full-time servant and may take private practice.
new.angle: U0302 notes gap: AG not in the Cabinet

new.s: For how many years was R. Venkataramani re-appointed Attorney General of India from 1 October 2025?
new.x: R. Venkataramani, AG since October 2022, was re-appointed for two years from 1 October 2025.
new.angle: U0302 notes gap: R. Venkataramani re-appointed 2025 for 2 years

new.s: Who is the second law officer of the Government of India?
new.x: The Attorney General is the first law officer and the Solicitor General, who assists him, is the second.
new.angle: U0302 notes gap: Solicitor General second law officer

new.s: In which year did Andhra Pradesh withdraw its 2020 resolution to abolish the Legislative Council?
new.x: The AP Assembly resolved in 2020 to abolish the Council again but withdrew the resolution in 2021.
new.angle: U0303 notes gap: AP Council abolition resolution withdrawn 2021

new.s: How many seats does the Legislative Assembly of Delhi have?
new.x: The Delhi Assembly, based on Article 239AA (69th Amendment, 1991), has 70 seats.
new.angle: U0303 notes gap: Delhi Assembly 70 seats

new.s: Which Articles of the Constitution deal with the State Legislature?
new.x: Part VI, Articles 168 to 212, deals with the State Legislature.
new.angle: U0303 notes gap: State Legislature Arts 168-212

new.s: Which Act introduced bicameral legislatures in some of the provinces?
new.x: The 1919 Act brought bicameralism at the Centre; the 1935 Act brought it in some provinces.
new.angle: U0303 notes gap: 1935 Act provincial bicameralism

new.s: How many members does Delhi elect to the Rajya Sabha?
new.x: Delhi elects 3 members to the Rajya Sabha, Puducherry 1 and Jammu and Kashmir 4.
new.angle: U0303 notes gap: Delhi 3 RS seats

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha?
new.x: Article 80 deals with the Council of States (Rajya Sabha); Article 81 with the Lok Sabha.
new.angle: U0304 notes gap: Article 80 composition of RS

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament?
new.x: Article 108 provides for a joint sitting of the two Houses.
new.angle: U0304 notes gap: Article 108 joint sitting

new.s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Andhra Pradesh have?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh has 25 Lok Sabha seats, 11 Rajya Sabha seats and 175 Assembly seats.
new.angle: U0304 notes gap: AP 25 Lok Sabha seats

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh has 25 seats in the Lok Sabha and 11 in the Rajya Sabha.
2. Telangana has 17 seats in the Lok Sabha and 7 in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: AP has 25 LS and 11 RS seats; Telangana has 17 LS and 7 RS seats.
new.angle: U0304 notes gap: AP/Telangana seats in both Houses

new.s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Maharashtra have?
new.x: Maharashtra has 48 Lok Sabha seats (and 19 in the Rajya Sabha).
new.angle: U0304 notes gap: Maharashtra 48 LS seats

new.s: In the Rajya Sabha polls of 18 June 2026 for 24 seats in 10 States, how many seats were from Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Of the 24 Rajya Sabha seats polled on 18 June 2026, 4 were from Andhra Pradesh.
new.angle: U0304 notes gap: 2026 RS polls - 4 AP seats

new.s: On the basis of which Census did the 87th Amendment provide for readjustment of constituencies?
new.x: The 87th Amendment based the readjustment of constituencies on the 2001 Census (Kuldip Singh Commission).
new.angle: U0304 notes gap: 87th Amendment - 2001 Census

new.s: Under Article 105(3), the uncodified privileges of the Houses of Parliament were historically those of which body?
new.x: Article 105(3) privileges are not codified; historically they were those of the British House of Commons.
new.angle: U0304 notes gap: privileges modelled on House of Commons

new.s: How many women members were there in the First Lok Sabha (1952)?
new.x: The 1st Lok Sabha had 22 women; the 6th had the lowest (19) and the 17th the highest (78).
new.angle: U0304 notes gap: 22 women in 1st Lok Sabha

new.s: On which date was the First Lok Sabha constituted after the first general elections?
new.x: The first Lok Sabha was duly constituted on 17 April 1952 after the general elections of 1951-52.
new.angle: U0304 web: first Lok Sabha constituted 17 April 1952 (PYQ yc1168beba52 angle)

new.s: In which year did the First Lok Sabha hold its first sitting?
new.x: The members of the first Lok Sabha met for the first time on 13 May 1952.
new.angle: U0304 web: first sitting of Lok Sabha 13 May 1952

new.s: Who was the first Deputy Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly (1956)?
new.x: In the first AP Legislature (1956) Kalluri Subbarao was Deputy Speaker; Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was Speaker.
new.angle: U0305 notes gap: first AP Deputy Speaker Kalluri Subbarao

new.s: Which Article provides that the Speaker shall not preside while a resolution for his removal is under consideration?
new.x: Article 96 bars the Speaker (or Deputy Speaker) from presiding during his own removal resolution; he may speak and vote in the first instance.
new.angle: U0305 notes gap: Article 96 own removal

new.s: On average, about how many sittings did State Legislative Assemblies hold in 2025?
new.x: State Assemblies averaged only about 24 sittings in 2025.
new.angle: U0305 notes gap: State Assemblies 24 sittings in 2025

new.s: Which Article provides for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly?
new.x: Article 178 provides for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of a State Assembly, as Article 93 does for the Lok Sabha.
new.angle: U0305 notes gap: Article 178 State Speaker/Deputy Speaker

new.s: When was President's Rule imposed in Andhra State after the Prakasam ministry fell by one vote?
new.x: After Gouthu Latchanna's no-confidence motion passed 69-68, President's Rule ran from 16 November 1954 to 27 March 1955.
new.angle: U0306 notes gap: President's Rule in Andhra State Nov 1954

new.s: In the 17th Lok Sabha, for about what share of its scheduled time did Question Hour function?
new.x: In the 17th Lok Sabha, Question Hour ran for only about 60% of its time.
new.angle: U0306 notes gap: 17th LS Question Hour 60%

new.s: What is a parliamentary committee on a Bill made up of members of one House only called?
new.x: A Select Committee has members of one House; a Joint Committee has members of both Houses.
new.angle: U0306 notes gap: Select Committee = one House

new.s: How many of the 24 Department-related Standing Committees function under the Lok Sabha?
new.x: Of the 24 DRSCs, 16 are under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha.
new.angle: U0306 notes gap: DRSCs 16 under LS

new.s: Who was the chairman of the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the 2G spectrum issue (2011)?
new.x: The 30-member 2G JPC (20 LS + 10 RS) was chaired by P.C. Chacko.
new.angle: U0306 notes gap: 2G JPC chairman P.C. Chacko

new.s: To which body was the FCRA (Amendment) Bill, 2026 sent in August 2026?
o: A Select Committee of the Rajya Sabha
new.x: The FCRA (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
new.angle: U0306 notes gap: FCRA Bill 2026 to JPC

new.s: How many members does the Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions have?
new.x: The Committee on Petitions has 15 members in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha.
new.angle: U0306 notes gap: RS Petitions Committee 10
